label: Epidemiology and outbreak investigation
description: The people who detect and investigate outbreaks: health department epidemiology and communicable disease programs, hospital infection prevention teams, public health laboratories and epidemiology programs. It describes the analytic work (case definitions, line lists, curves, contact follow-up, laboratory turnaround). The health department as an agency (operations center, health orders, dispensing) is the public health profile, which this one extends.

vocabulary.facility: the epidemiology program (surveillance unit, investigation team, the laboratory and, for a hospital, the infection prevention office)
vocabulary.public: residents, exposed contacts, patients, families and the communities the program serves
vocabulary.frontline: epidemiologists, disease investigators, contact tracers, infection preventionists, laboratory scientists, data analysts
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the outbreak response team's command post or the departmental operations center (DOC)

it: reportable disease surveillance and case management system (e.g. NBS or a commercial platform)
electronic laboratory reporting (ELR) and electronic case reporting (eCR) feeds
outbreak investigation forms and line lists (Epi Info, REDCap or a spreadsheet)
molecular typing and sequence-sharing networks for foodborne and respiratory pathogens
Health Alert Network messaging and partner mass notification
hospital infection surveillance software and the electronic health record
public website, data dashboards and the hotline
shared services: email, directory and SIEM
ot: public health laboratory biosafety cabinets and directional airflow
-80 °C freezers with alarms and specimen cold chain
vaccine refrigerators with remote temperature monitoring

roles.name: State Epidemiologist / Epidemiology Program Director
roles.description: Declares an outbreak, approves the case definition in use, requests CDC Epi-Aid and decides what data are released publicly.

roles.name: Local Epidemiologist / Communicable Disease Lead
roles.description: Sets investigation priorities, case tiers (confirmed, probable, suspect), contact categories and worker exclusion recommendations.

roles.name: Disease Investigator / Contact Tracer
roles.description: Interviews cases, classifies contacts by exposure window, keeps the follow-up schedule and escalates unreachable contacts.

roles.name: Surveillance Epidemiologist / Data Analyst
roles.description: Owns the line list, the epidemic curve by onset date, rates and the numbers every message must match.

roles.name: Environmental Health Specialist
roles.description: Inspects food sources, runs the traceback and recommends restaurant or facility closure.

roles.name: Public Health Laboratory Director
roles.description: Sets testing priorities and specimen acceptance, manages turnaround and referral for confirmation and typing.

roles.name: Infection Preventionist
roles.description: Applies isolation precautions, assesses staff and patient exposure, recommends unit closure and reports to the health department.

roles.name: Hospital Epidemiologist / Infectious Disease Physician
roles.description: Reviews cases clinically and advises on treatment and prophylaxis recommendations.

roles.name: Health Officer
roles.description: Issues isolation, quarantine and closure orders on the epidemiologists' recommendation (the public health profile).

roles.name: Epidemiology Student / Epidemic Intelligence Service Officer
roles.team: Team F: Field Team and Academic Program
roles.description: Works field tasks under supervision: questionnaires, line list entry, hypothesis tables. In a teaching exercise this role is the learner.

roles.name: Informatics Lead
roles.description: Owns the surveillance and contact tracing systems, ELR and eCR feeds and the access controls on contact lists.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Writes exposure notices, health alerts and press statements that match the numbers on the curve, and counters rumors.

outsideParties: CDC (Epi-Aid, the Emergency Operations Center, foodborne, respiratory and vaccine-preventable disease programs)
neighboring health jurisdictions and the state health department
the state public health laboratory and reference laboratories
FDA and USDA FSIS (food traceback and recalls)
school districts and child care centers
airlines and the airport authority (exposure notification)
employers and congregate settings (nursing homes, shelters, camps)
clinicians, urgent care centers, pharmacies and hospital infection preventionists
mediaChannels: a local TV health reporter's email
a school district email to parents
a viral post naming the wrong restaurant

sceneAnchors.public: a crowded urgent care waiting room: parents with children, a masked receptionist at a sliding window, hand-sanitizer stations, handwritten signs, daylight through a front window
sceneAnchors.control: an outbreak response room: epidemiologists at long tables with laptops, a whiteboard with a hand-drawn epidemic curve, printed line lists and a map with pins, fluorescent lighting
sceneAnchors.exterior: a restaurant kitchen entrance at the back of a strip mall, an environmental health inspector with a clipboard and a cooler, a dumpster and wet pavement under overcast sky

addedThreatFamilies.label: Foodborne outbreak
addedThreatFamilies.description: Illness spreads among people who shared a meal or a food source; the team works from the first complaints to the vehicle, the control and the public message.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: A cluster appears through an ordinary channel and nobody is sure it is more than coincidence.
beats: Two complaints to the health department hotline or a restaurant inspector about illness after the same event
An unrelated noise report the surveillance team must set aside
A clinician calls about several patients with similar symptoms

phaseArc.title: Verify and define cases
phaseArc.goal: The team confirms the diagnosis, decides whether this is an outbreak and writes a working case definition.
beats: A first laboratory result that confirms or does not confirm a pathogen
A request to adopt a case definition before the line list is large
Pressure from the venue to say it was not their food

phaseArc.title: Describe by time, place and person
phaseArc.goal: The epidemic curve and the line list tell a story the team must read correctly; onset date, not report date, drives the curve.
beats: A line list with some late reports and some missing onset dates
A curve that looks like a point source, with a few cases outside the expected window
A secondary case that does not fit the common-source story

phaseArc.title: Hypothesis
phaseArc.goal: Attack rates and odds ratios by food item point to a vehicle, with distractors that are plausible.
beats: A table of exposures where two items look close
A food handler who was ill before the event

phaseArc.title: Control
phaseArc.goal: The team acts before the investigation is complete: exclusion, closure or recall, each with a cost.
beats: Recommendation to exclude ill food workers
A decision to close the facility or wait for the confirmatory result
A supplier recall that crosses jurisdictions

phaseArc.title: Communicate
phaseArc.goal: Every message matches the numbers on the curve and the same advice reaches the public, clinicians and the venue.
beats: A press release draft whose case count differs from the line list
Misinformation naming the wrong establishment

phaseArc.title: Close and after-action
phaseArc.goal: The outbreak is declared over on a stated rule and the lessons are recorded.
beats: Two incubation periods without a new case
A hot wash disagreement about when the case definition should have changed

decisionPointExamples: close the establishment on a probable vehicle now, or wait a day for the laboratory result and risk more cases
issue a public notice naming the event, or hold it until the traceback is complete
request CDC Epi-Aid, or work with local staff only
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a line list entry with an onset time, a food history that two cases share, a laboratory result or a typing match, an inspection finding, a worker who reported illness
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the surveillance system is slow, interviews are unreachable, the laboratory backlog delays the result, the venue's guest list is incomplete
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the environmental health team, the public health laboratory, the venue or caterer and, for a recall, FDA or USDA FSIS
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of public health response decisions: case definitions, counts, onset dates, exposures, control measures and messages. Give no pathogen culture, growth or handling detail.

decisionMustMention.description: a control or communication decision (exclusion, closure, recall, notice or the case definition)

addedThreatFamilies.label: Respiratory pathogen with community spread
addedThreatFamilies.description: A respiratory illness rises in the community; the team decides how to define cases, which measures to recommend and when, and how to keep messages consistent.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: Indicators rise before a name is agreed: visits, laboratory positives, school absences.
beats: A syndromic indicator above baseline
A school reports absences
A wastewater activity level moves up one category

phaseArc.title: Verify and define cases
phaseArc.goal: The team writes a case definition with confirmed, probable and suspect tiers and sets the testing priority.
beats: A laboratory with limited capacity asks which specimens to prioritize
A hospital and the health department define a case differently

phaseArc.title: Describe and decide
phaseArc.goal: The curve keeps rising while the team weighs measures with a cost for each.
beats: A projection with a stated reproduction number the team treats as certain
A request from an employer for exclusion guidance
A neighboring county changes its recommendation

phaseArc.title: Control and communicate
phaseArc.goal: Measures start, the public message must match the numbers and advice stays the same across partners.
beats: A health alert to clinicians and a different school letter
A social post claiming the numbers are hidden

decisionPointExamples: recommend a measure now on early data, or wait for another reporting cycle and risk a steeper curve
narrow testing to the highest-risk groups, or keep broad testing and accept longer turnaround
release the dashboard figures with caveats, or hold them until the reporting delay settles
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a laboratory positivity trend, an age shift in cases, an absenteeism figure, a wastewater level change, a cluster in a congregate setting
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: reporting delays, a laboratory instrument down, staff shortages in the investigation team, a dashboard that disagrees with the line list
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the state health department, the hospitals' infection preventionists and the school districts
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Describe disease spread only as numbers, curves and response decisions. Never describe how to grow, modify or spread any pathogen.

decisionMustMention.description: a public health recommendation, testing, alert or data release decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Vaccine-preventable disease exposure
addedThreatFamilies.description: A case of a vaccine-preventable disease such as measles was in public places while infectious; the team builds an exposure list and decides on notification and post-exposure measures.

phaseArc.title: Report
phaseArc.goal: A clinician reports a suspected case and the infectious period must be worked out from the onset date.
beats: A call from an urgent care about a suspected case with travel history
A specimen sent for confirmation with a turnaround the team must manage

phaseArc.title: Exposure list
phaseArc.goal: Places and people the case visited while infectious are listed, with windows computed from onset and the infectious period.
beats: A flight, a school and a clinic waiting room all on the itinerary
A contact list that grows each day and includes unreachable contacts

phaseArc.title: Notify and protect
phaseArc.goal: Notices, immunity checks and exclusions go out with exact places and time windows.
beats: An exposure notice draft with the wrong window
A school asks which students must stay home and for how long

phaseArc.title: Monitor and close
phaseArc.goal: Contacts are followed through the incubation window and the response closes on a stated rule.
beats: A second case among contacts
A decision to stop monitoring

decisionPointExamples: publish an exposure notice naming the flight and the school now, or confirm the laboratory result first
exclude unvaccinated students for the full window, or allow return after post-exposure vaccination as the recommendation permits
classify a brief waiting-room overlap as a close contact or not
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an itinerary detail, a vaccination record, a seating chart, a laboratory result, a contact who cannot be reached
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: an incomplete passenger list from the airline, immunization registry gaps, contacts out of the jurisdiction, a hotline overwhelmed
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the airline and airport, the school district, the clinic and neighboring health departments
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Exposure windows are computed from the onset date and the infectious period of the disease; show the arithmetic in the controller notes and keep every notice consistent with it.

decisionMustMention.description: an exposure notice, exclusion, contact classification or vaccination decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Healthcare-associated infection cluster
addedThreatFamilies.description: Infections link patients in the same unit or procedure; infection prevention and the health department work the cluster and disagree on when to act.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: Infection preventionists notice more cases than expected on one unit.
beats: A surveillance report of three similar infections in a week on one unit
A noise item about an unrelated isolation room alarm

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The hospital and the health department define cases together and review exposures: procedures, devices, staff and rooms.
beats: A shared device or procedure appears in several charts
The hospital prefers to investigate quietly; the health department wants the report now

phaseArc.title: Control
phaseArc.goal: Precautions, cohorting, screening and possibly closing a unit, each with an operating cost.
beats: A recommendation to stop admissions to the unit
A staffing shortage when staff are furloughed for exposure

phaseArc.title: Communicate and close
phaseArc.goal: Patients, families, staff and the public hear consistent messages and the cluster is closed on a stated rule.
beats: A family hears about the cluster from the press first
A decision to reopen the unit

decisionPointExamples: close the unit to admissions on a probable link now, or keep it open with added precautions and risk more cases
notify affected patients and families now, or wait until the investigation identifies a source
share the hospital's line list with the health department in full, or only the minimum required
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a shared procedure or device, a room history, a staff assignment sheet, a screening result, a typing match between isolates
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: an incomplete room history, screening swabs delayed, staff shortages, disagreement about which tier a case belongs in
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the infection preventionist, the hospital epidemiologist and the health department
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep to infection prevention and public health response decisions; do not describe clinical procedures in detail.

decisionMustMention.description: a unit, isolation, screening, notification or reporting decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Mass prophylaxis or vaccination dispensing
addedThreatFamilies.description: A dispensing site must open and keep throughput against a plan; the team decides on sites, hours, eligibility and the queue.

phaseArc.title: Activate
phaseArc.goal: The decision to dispense is made and the site opens against a clock.
beats: The decision to open sites with an eligibility rule
Staff and supplies arrive late at one site

phaseArc.title: Operate
phaseArc.goal: Arrivals exceed station capacity and the queue grows.
beats: A queue of hundreds before opening
A station is short of forms or staff

phaseArc.title: Adjust
phaseArc.goal: The team re-balances stations, hours and sites using throughput and queue data.
beats: Throughput is below plan at one site
A call to widen eligibility under pressure

phaseArc.title: Close and report
phaseArc.goal: Sites close on a stated rule and the numbers are reported.
beats: Leftover supplies and the accountability count
A message about the remaining supply that must match the totals

decisionPointExamples: open a second site with thin staffing now, or add stations at the first site and accept a longer queue
widen eligibility to relieve pressure, or hold the stated priority groups
close a site at the posted hour with a queue outside, or extend and strain staff
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a throughput count, a queue length report, a station staffing sheet, a supply count
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a late delivery, a cold chain alarm, a short-staffed station, a registration system outage
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the medical countermeasure coordinator, county emergency management, law enforcement for site security and the Medical Reserve Corps
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use throughput as people per hour per station and queue length over time; do not invent clinical dosing detail.

decisionMustMention.description: a site, station, queue, eligibility or staffing decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Surveillance signal
addedThreatFamilies.description: A wastewater, syndromic or laboratory signal appears before clinical reports; the team decides whether and how to act on it.

phaseArc.title: Signal
phaseArc.goal: An indicator crosses a threshold; the cause is not known.
beats: A wastewater activity level rises from low to high in a sewershed
A syndromic count above the expected range

phaseArc.title: Verify
phaseArc.goal: The team checks data quality before acting: a lab change, a reporting delay, a data entry error.
beats: A sampling site change that may explain the rise
A clinic reports no unusual visits

phaseArc.title: Decide and inform
phaseArc.goal: The team decides on a public or clinician notice with caveats.
beats: A reporter asks about the signal
A neighboring jurisdiction sees the same pattern

phaseArc.title: Follow
phaseArc.goal: Clinical indicators confirm or do not confirm the signal.
beats: Cases appear a week later
The signal fades without cases and the team explains why

decisionPointExamples: alert clinicians now on the wastewater signal alone, or wait for a second indicator
publish the sewershed level publicly with caveats, or hold until the next sample
start targeted testing in the affected area, or watch for another week
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a second site's level, a laboratory positivity change, a school absence count, a sampling note
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a delayed sample, a laboratory method change, a dashboard lag, a data gap at a site
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the wastewater utility, the state laboratory and the neighboring health departments
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Levels are shown with the dataset's own category names; never present a simulated series as real.

decisionMustMention.description: an alert, notice, publication or testing decision on the signal

addedThreatFamilies.label: Laboratory surge
addedThreatFamilies.description: Specimen volume exceeds laboratory capacity; the team sets testing priorities and manages turnaround, referral and communication.

phaseArc.title: Rising volume
phaseArc.goal: Specimens arrive faster than the laboratory can run them.
beats: A hospital courier drops twice the usual specimens
Turnaround rises above its target

phaseArc.title: Prioritize
phaseArc.goal: The laboratory and epidemiologists agree on which specimens come first.
beats: A hospital requests priority for its patients
An outbreak-linked set of specimens arrives with chain of custody

phaseArc.title: Relieve
phaseArc.goal: Referral, overtime and reagent decisions with a cost on both sides.
beats: A reagent shortage
A request to send specimens to a reference laboratory with a longer transport time

phaseArc.title: Recover
phaseArc.goal: The backlog clears and the laboratory reports turnaround plainly to partners.
beats: A partner complains about delays
A final turnaround report

decisionPointExamples: reject non-priority specimens to protect turnaround, or accept all and delay every result
refer a batch to a reference laboratory, or run overtime and keep control of results
tell clinicians to restrict testing, or keep testing open and accept the delay
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a received, pending and positive count, a turnaround figure against target, an instrument downtime note
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: an instrument fault, a reagent shortage, a staff gap, an interface failure that drops results
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the clinical laboratories, hospitals, the courier service and the reference laboratory
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep to specimen counts, turnaround and priorities; give no laboratory method detail for any dangerous agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a testing priority, referral or turnaround decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Surveillance service degradation
addedThreatFamilies.description: A surveillance system outage, a laboratory reporting backlog or a contact list breach degrades the investigation while the outbreak continues.

phaseArc.title: Degradation
phaseArc.goal: A feed or system fails quietly and counts stop matching.
beats: The electronic laboratory reporting feed stops delivering
A helpdesk ticket from the investigation team

phaseArc.title: Impact
phaseArc.goal: The curve and the line list diverge and decisions rest on stale numbers.
beats: A dashboard that does not update
A manual line list started in a spreadsheet

phaseArc.title: Workaround
phaseArc.goal: The team chooses between manual methods and waiting, and decides what to tell partners.
beats: A paper reporting fallback
A report that a contact list was exposed

phaseArc.title: Recover and reconcile
phaseArc.goal: Data are reconciled and the numbers in earlier messages are corrected where wrong.
beats: A backlog of results lands at once and the curve jumps
A correction notice

decisionPointExamples: keep reporting counts with a stated delay, or pause the public dashboard until data are reconciled
notify contacts of a list exposure now, or confirm the scope first
move to a paper line list, or wait for the system to return
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a system log entry, a gap in daily counts, a vendor status note, a duplicated record
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a vendor restoration time, a manual process that doubles workload, mismatched counts between teams
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the surveillance system vendor, the state health department and the privacy officer
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Exercise data only; contact lists in the scenario are fictional and marked as exercise material.

decisionMustMention.description: a reporting, notification, reconciliation or manual-process decision

noiseExamples: a restaurant owner disputing an inspection score
a reporter asking about last year's flu numbers
a laboratory courier running late for an unrelated panel
a spreadsheet macro that stopped working
pressureExamples: a venue's lawyer demanding the department not name the event
a viral post naming the wrong restaurant as the source
a school board member asking why the school was not told first
a reporter asking whether the department is hiding cases
a hospital executive asking the health department to delay a unit closure notice
